findings.description: F-003: `pygbag igra.py` (build_chapter_20.py:2366-2371) was a non-working command. pygbag requires the entry file to be named main.py -- official wiki: 'Name the file with your game loop main.py'; README: '"your.app.folder" must contain a main.py'. Verified against pygbag 0.9.3 in an isolated venv: `python -m pygbag --build igratest/igra.py` exits 0 with no error and packs assets/igra.py, while the generated build/web/index.html contains `main = appdir / "assets" / "main.py"` at line 60 -- so the bundle builds 'successfully' and then does nothing in the browser. The control build with the file renamed to main.py packs assets/main.py and matches.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: the command became `pygbag moya_igra/` (a folder, per official usage), the following sentence now says the argument is a folder rather than a single file, and a new warning callout «Файл с игровым циклом обязан называться main.py» explains that pygbag looks for exactly that name, that a differently-named entry point makes the build succeed silently while the browser page stays blank, and that a blank page after a successful build means checking the filename first. Verified after rebuild: «pygbag igra.py» returns 0 files and «pygbag moya_igra/» returns 1.

findings.description: F-013: «async def main() с await asyncio.sleep(0) вместо clock.tick() в чистом виде» (build_chapter_20.py:2397-2400) said the await replaces clock.tick(). The official pygbag wiki keeps both -- its canonical loop is `clock.tick(60); pygame.display.update(); await asyncio.sleep(0)` with the note 'Right after your clock.tick() is fine'. The section's own comparison table one paragraph earlier was correct; only the parenthetical contradicted it.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: now «await asyncio.sleep(0) в конце каждого кадра», followed by an explicit sentence that the await is added *рядом с* clock.tick() rather than replacing it, since pygbag's own examples keep the frame-rate cap and put the await straight after it. Verified present in the rebuilt 20-30-publikatsiya-veb.html.

findings.description: F-016: «Производительность браузерной сборки не гарантированно ниже десктопной величиной, которую можно назвать заранее — ... и её стоит измерять ... а не считать её заранее ниже...» (build_chapter_20.py:2400-2403) did not parse, and repeated «её» within one clause.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: replaced with two clean sentences — «Насколько браузерная сборка медленнее настольной, заранее сказать нельзя: это зависит от браузера, устройства игрока и самой игры. Производительность стоит измерять на целевом устройстве, а не закладывать какой-то определённый процент потерь заранее.» Verified after rebuild: «не гарантированно ниже» returns 0 files and «заранее сказать нельзя» returns 1.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Shows how to publish the game to the browser with pygbag, and explains what differs in the browser sandbox -- filesystem access, the async main loop, performance.

pygbag is a community project, not an official part of pygame-ce. -- Confirmed -- pygame-web/pygbag is a separate organisation from pygame-community/pygame-ce, with its own release cadence (0.9.3, 2026-02-12). The warning callout is accurate.

`pygbag igra.py` builds and serves the game. -- Was FALSE -- pygbag requires the entry point to be named main.py. Built for real with pygbag 0.9.3: `python -m pygbag --build igratest/igra.py` exits 0 and packs assets/igra.py, but the generated index.html boot code hardcodes `main = appdir / "assets" / "main.py"`, so nothing runs. Fixed under F-003.

The browser build needs an async main loop with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` each frame. -- Confirmed -- the pygbag wiki emphasises `await asyncio.sleep(0)  # Very important, and keep it 0`. But the chapter said it replaces clock.tick(), whereas the official example keeps both. Fixed under F-013.

Browser filesystem access is restricted by the sandbox and performance must be measured on the target device rather than assumed. -- Confirmed -- both correct, and the refusal to quote a fixed slowdown percentage is the right call.
